paper.title_en: Fermi lune and non-reciprocal transport in rhombohedral multilayer graphene
paper.abstract_en: We develop a microscopic theory of Fermi-lune metals in rhombohedral multilayer graphene and investigate their non-reciprocal longitudinal transport. We show that tuning the layer number and displacement field drives Lifshitz transitions from circular to annular non-interacting Fermi surfaces accompanied by redistributions of electronic weight among layers. Combining renormalization-group corrections with unrestricted Hartree-Fock calculations, we further demonstrate how Coulomb interactions reconstruct the non-interacting annular Fermi surface into crescent-shaped Fermi lune through spontaneous breaking of time-reversal, mirror and rotation symmetries. We determine competing mean-field phases for four to nine layers and distinguish two types of transdimensional orbital magnetic orders. Beyond the Fermi-lune state that exhibits transdimensional anomalous Hall effect reported recently, we also identify a mirror-preserving Fermi-lune phase with spontaneous in-plane orbital magnetization but a symmetry-forbidden anomalous Hall response. The maximum calculated in-plane orbital moment increases approximately linearly with layer number. The asymmetric Fermi-velocity distributions of these states also lead to intrinsic non-reciprocal longitudinal transport. Measurements presented here in a nine-layer device show a non-reciprocal resistance ratio reaching 23% at a current magnitude of 17 nA. These results elucidate the formation mechanism, competing symmetries, and thickness dependence of Fermi-lune states, and connect their electronic structure to a longitudinal-transport signature beyond the previously reported anomalous Hall phenomenology.
